bull_bear.body: Dividend payout: 50% of PAT; CAPEX funded by Rs. 2,000cr reserves + state-backed credit line; Debt expected from FY27 end; No equity dilution planned; Focus on internal accruals and state financing
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Land acquisition delays; Statutory clearance bottlenecks; Spares import delays (power plant); Underground mining execution risk (first in Western India); Copper and rare earths technology risk; Volatility in coal/lignite pricing; Regulatory delays in PPA pass-through
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, long-term oriented, transparent on delays; acknowledges execution challenges but reaffirms 2030 targets; emphasizes state support, technical rigor, and patient capital; avoids overpromising on near-term volumes
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: GMDC's lignite pricing is now only 10-15% below Indonesian coal (down from 60-70% in FY21), indicating strong competitive positioning; Power plant CAPEX of Rs. 300-400cr is not a loss but a deferred investment with regulatory pass-through; Land acquisition (46% of CAPEX) is the true bottleneck, not technology or mining expertise
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Lignite: 8MTPA FY25 (down from 10MTPA target); 10-15% growth FY26 from 4 existing mines; New mines (Lakhpat, Walia, Damlai) to contribute from FY27; Coal: Baitarani West (15MTPA) to break ground in FY25, first production ~1MTPA in FY26, ramp to 5MTPA by FY28; Copper: Ambaji underground mine, first production FY28; Rare Earths: LOI received, commercialization in 2-3 years; Bauxite: 5MTPA, contributing Rs. 80-100cr revenue; Power: ATPS plant delayed due to spares, new PPA signed with 30paise/kWh price increase, pass-through for Rs. 300-400cr CAPEX

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 10-15% FY26 (lignite), +50%+ from coal/copper by FY27; Margin: Lignite margins stable at ~25%, coal margins lower but volume-driven; Order inflow: None; Capex/commissioning: FY26-27: Rs. 2,000-2,500cr/year; Baitarani West coal mine groundbreaking in FY25, first production FY26; Copper project commissioning FY28

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: GMDC is transitioning from a regional lignite miner to a national-scale critical minerals player, with Odisha coal and Copper Project Ambaji as key growth drivers; volume growth is delayed but long-term capacity expansion remains intact, with 15MTPA lignite and 15MTPA coal targets by 2035.

open.item: Effective tax rate from FY23 onwards will be in the range of 25%-26% under the new regime.
Mission 2000 aims to take the number of active customers in excess of 2,000 over the year.
Targeting 10%-15% volume growth in FY26 from the four existing lignite mines (off an FY25 base of 8 million tons).
Bauxite mines (Saurashtra and Kutch) now all contributing, expected to generate significant revenue of Rs.80-100 crore.

ATPS thermal plant overhaul running behind schedule due to imported spares delays; expected to turn to a better future this year with new PPA (power ~30 paisa costlier) and Rs.300-400 crore capex recovered as pass-through.
Baitarani-West coal block (15 MTPA peak, top-12/13 in country) groundbreaking expected this year (FY26) with ~1 million tons in first year, ramping quickly to 3 then 5 million tons.
Burapahar coal mine staggered by a year behind Baitarani-West; exploring underground coal gasification partners (blue hydrogen) via a live EOI.
Six new lignite mines (flag bearers Lakhpat, Walia, Damlai) undergoing statutory clearances; volumes expected FY27 onwards, not FY26.
No debt expected in FY26 and most of FY27; debt to start being taken towards the end of FY27, funded by ~Rs.2,000 crore reserves and a line of credit.
Copper Project Ambaji (first underground mine in Western India) to see results in 2 to 3 years, with revenue realistically around FY28.
Capex distribution: Rs.3,000-4,000 crore critical minerals, Rs.4,000 crore coal, Rs.3,000 crore new lignite plus Rs.1,000 crore-plus existing lignite.
Total capex journey of Rs.13,000 crore-plus by 2030 (46% land, 15% R&R, 30% plant & machinery), steady ~Rs.1,500-2,000 crore/year peaking in two years.
Holding on to the Project Shikhar 2030 target of ~Rs.14,500 crore revenue (4x from ~Rs.2,800 crore now), acknowledging a possible few-quarters shift.
Targeting lignite production of 15 million tons by 2035 (70% from new mines, 30% from existing which continue contributing until 2030).
Coal (Odisha) to have slightly lower margins but higher volumes; government revenue share 30% for one mine and 40% for the other.
Cumulative capacity of all three Odisha coal blocks is 26 million tons per annum, all coal going towards Gujarat energy security.
Signed MoU with GUVNL to jointly develop up to 4,400 MW of thermal power, GMDC operationalizing coal blocks and GUVNL putting up thermal assets.
Under board mandate, coal blocks target an IRR of 15%, never going below 12%.
Will embark on digitizing mines using IoT devices to control variable costs and improve mining efficiency, with action expected in the coming year.
In seven years, ambition for at least 40%-50% of revenues to come from opportunities other than lignite.

verdicts.item: GMDC nominated preferred allottee for Ambadongar Rare Earth project; looking at a 3-year horizon for the project.
verdicts.note: 'We have received an LOI. Work is going on for the next stages' - Ambadongar RE project advancing on the multi-year horizon.

verdicts.item: Fluorspar plant refurbishing started, targeting a trial run by 15th August 2023 and commencing production by Q4 FY24.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY24

verdicts.item: In the coming three to four years production should go up to 14-15 million tonnes, currently limited to Gujarat.
verdicts.note: '15 million tons by 2035' - the 14-15M-in-3-4-years target pushed well out.

verdicts.item: Live RFPs floated to significantly expand capacity of the Bhavnagar project to help achieve volume targets.
verdicts.note: 'one package was operational and the second was supposed to get operational... because of delay in land acquisition... that has been resolved now' - expansion partly live, ramp continuing.

verdicts.item: Six new mines to be operationalized within the next two financial years, with RFPs for MDOs/turnkey contracts coming soon.
verdicts.note: new mines 'undergoing various stages of statutory clearances... volumes next year onwards' - not operationalized within the original two-FY horizon.

verdicts.item: BCG Phase-I complete; acting on process/marketing/governance improvements now, with larger diversification initiatives (limestone, silica sand, multi-metal) to be updated subsequently.
verdicts.note: 'the capital and revenue journey up till 2030 is planned, that entire model gets reworked every quarter' - continuing implementation.

verdicts.item: Bauxite pilot beneficiation to commence by end-February 2023, targeting around 0.88 million tons of bauxite disposal next financial year (FY24).
verdicts.note: 'we have done some 5x tons of Bauxite... all these mines are contributing revenues' - bauxite disposal progressing (exact 0.88M FY24 figure not stated). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: EBITDA per ton close to Rs.1,800-1,900 this quarter expected to sustain if the price differential to imported coal holds.
verdicts.note: 'pricing was somewhere around Rs. 3,400 per ton. And on that we are making some EBITDA of around Rs. 800 to Rs. 890 per ton' (uncontested) - well below the Rs.1,800-1,900 that was to be sustained.

verdicts.item: No plans for share buyback; company is in expansion and aggressive mode deploying reserves into six new lignite projects.
verdicts.note: 'This journey till 2030, we have planned for a CAPEX in the range of Rs. 13,000 crore' - expansion continues, no buyback (50% dividend payout).

verdicts.item: Plan to increase lignite capacity from 80 lakh to 110 lakh tons over the next couple of years.
verdicts.note: 'we expect to see lignite production in the range of 15 million tons... 15 million tons by 2035' - capacity expansion reaffirmed (now a longer horizon). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Bauxite and manganese JV offtake expected to improve this year via open-auction sales, beneficiation and better JV partner handholding.
verdicts.note: 'all these mines are contributing revenues... Rs. 80 crore-Rs. 90 crore-Rs. 100 crore' - bauxite offtake improved; manganese not detailed.

verdicts.item: Lakhpat to be the first new mine to roll off, with groundbreaking in three to four of the new projects during FY24 (Lakhpat, one more in Kutch, two in South Gujarat).
verdicts.note: new mines 'undergoing various stages of statutory clearances... volumes next year onwards' - FY24 groundbreaking of Lakhpat/new projects not delivered.

wtt.summary: 0% guidance hit (7 chains); 2/18 projects on-time; 5 expired; 25% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident but candid about slippage; management owned that FY25 fell short of 10 MT (Rajpardi safety closure, Bhavnagar land delay) and that only Rs.644 crore of the planned Rs.3,000 crore FY25 capex was spent, while holding 2030 targets.

meta.thesis: GMDC is transitioning from a regional lignite miner to a national-scale critical minerals player, with Odisha coal and Copper Project Ambaji as key growth drivers; volume growth is delayed but long-term capacity expansion remains intact, with 15MTPA lignite and 15MTPA coal targets by 2035.
